questions.passage: In his Critique of Judgment, Immanuel Kant distinguished beautiful arts from pleasant arts. He described pleasant arts as “those that are directed merely to enjoyment. Of this class are all those charming arts that can gratify a company at table…to this class belong all games which bring with them no further interest than that of making the time pass imperceptibly.”
questions.prompt: How does Kant characterize pleasant arts in the quoted passage?
options: As directed merely toward enjoyment and making time pass unnoticed.
As necessarily changing every person’s moral beliefs.
As devoid of any capacity to please people together.
As a scientific test of the psychological effects of games.
questions.promptZh: Kant 的引语怎样界定 pleasant arts？
optionsZh: 仅以享受、让时间不知不觉流逝为方向。
必定改变每个人的道德信念。
完全不能使聚在一起的人愉悦。
检验游戏心理效果的科学实验。
analyses: A merely to enjoyment 与 time pass imperceptibly 直接支持。
B no further interest 不能加上必定改变信念。
C gratify a company at table 指让同桌人愉悦。
D 这是哲学分类引述，不是实验。仅在此分类中解释 pleasant，不推成所有游戏绝无其他价值。

questions.passage: In contrast, “beautiful art is a mode of representation which is purposive for itself, and which, although devoid of [definite] purpose, yet furthers the culture of the mental powers in reference to social communication.” Here, Kant defines an aesthetic experience as something greater than the enjoyment of mere sensation but rather the enjoyment of what he calls “reflective judgment,” which involves some gap between sensation and reality and a new mental representation and understanding of an object.
questions.prompt: What distinguishes reflective judgment from mere sensation here?
options: It excludes any mental representation of an object.
It is simply the same as passing time pleasantly.
It involves a gap between sensation and reality and a new mental understanding.
It guarantees that all viewers perceive an object identically.
questions.promptZh: 这里的反思判断与单纯感觉有什么区别？
optionsZh: 排除对对象的任何心理表征。
仅等同于愉快打发时间。
涉及感觉与现实的差距，以及新的心理理解。
保证所有观众理解完全一致。
analyses: A a new mental representation 明确保留表征。
B greater than...mere sensation 表示不止消遣。
C gap...new mental representation and understanding 是末尾解释。
D 没有人人一致的保证。purposive 与 devoid of definite purpose 并列是哲学限定，不擅自删括号或改成无任何意义。

evidence.quote: “reflective judgment,” which involves some gap between sensation and reality and a new mental representation and understanding of an object.

vocabulary.context: 在本书对 Kant 的阐释中，指不止感官愉悦、会重新理解对象的判断

questions.passage: When Sonny Rollins, the legendary jazz saxophonist, was asked about art and, more specifically, why art matters, his reply evoked Kantian aesthetic judgments: “Technology is no savior. We can eat, sleep, look at screens, make money—all aspects of our physical existence—but that doesn’t mean anything. Art is the exact opposite. It’s infinite, and without it, the world wouldn’t exist as it does.
questions.prompt: What contrast does Rollins draw between physical existence and art?
options: Technology guarantees that every life has meaning.
Art is simply another way to earn money and watch screens.
Meeting physical needs alone does not supply the significance he attributes to art.
Physical existence is described as impossible without modern screens.
questions.promptZh: Rollins 如何对比物质生存与艺术？
optionsZh: 科技保证每个人生有意义。
艺术只是赚钱和看屏幕的另一方式。
仅满足物质需要，并不具有他赋予艺术的意义。
没有现代屏幕就不可能生存。
analyses: A Technology is no savior 否定这种保证。
B exact opposite 表明对照，不是等同赚钱看屏幕。
C physical existence...doesn’t mean anything 后转向艺术，概括其价值判断。
D 举例生活活动不等于没有屏幕无法生存。这是 Rollins 的艺术观，不是作者实验得出的普遍生存定律。

Art matters today more than ever because it outlives the contentious political veneer that is cast over everything…. Art, in the same way, both inspires us to go out and find something new and highlights what we don’t know.”
questions.prompt: Which qualities are linked to 'the immaterial soul' in the quotation?
questions.promptZh: 引文把哪些特征与 immaterial soul 联系起来？
options: Food, sleep, screens, and income as physical necessities alone.
The proven absence of emotion from artistic experience.
Intuition and what people feel in their hearts.
An instruction that every artwork must have a fixed market price.
optionsZh: 只有饮食睡眠屏幕收入等物质需要。
艺术体验中已证明没有情感。
直觉与人们心中的感受。
每件艺术须有固定市价的指令。
analyses: A 是前一短段物质生存的列举，不能替换此处非物质意涵。
B feel in our hearts 明确情感，并非无情感。
C 冒号后 intuition、that which... 解释这一引述表达。
D 没有定价指令；soul 为艺术观的表达，不当成科学发现的实体或实验结论。

vocabulary.context: 在 immaterial soul 中不是另一常见义不重要的，而指精神层面。
vocabulary.example: The essay focused on immaterial aspects of the experience.

questions.passage: In his essay “The Power of Art in a Political Age,” David Brooks echoes Sonny Rollins’s point. Brooks writes, “Like a lot of people, I spend too much of my time enmeshed in politics…. So I’m trying to take countermeasures. I flee to the arts.”
questions.prompt: What does Brooks say he is trying to counteract?
options: Spending too much time learning a musical instrument.
A complete lack of interest in any public issue.
His inability to find any works of art.
Being too caught up in politics.
questions.promptZh: Brooks 说自己试图应对什么？
optionsZh: 学乐器耗时太多。
完全不关心公共议题。
找不到任何艺术作品。
过度卷入政治。
analyses: A 没有乐器学习的信息。
B enmeshed in politics 表示卷入过多，非毫不关心。
C I flee to the arts 指转向艺术，未说找不到。
D too much...enmeshed in politics 与 countermeasures 前后对应。这是文章作者的自述，不是建议所有人忽视政治。

evidence.quote: I spend too much of my time enmeshed in politics

vocabulary.context: Brooks 描述被政治占据过多时间
vocabulary.example: She became enmeshed in arguments that distracted her from her work.

questions.prompt: What does 'I flee to the arts' convey in Brooks's quotation?
questions.promptZh: Brooks 引文中 I flee to the arts 表达什么？
options: He physically moves to another country whose name is Arts.
He turns to art as an escape from excessive political entanglement.
He abandons art in order to increase political involvement.
He instructs every reader to stop all public engagement permanently.
optionsZh: 实际迁到一个名叫 Arts 的国家。
转向艺术，以摆脱过多政治纠缠。
离开艺术以增加政治投入。

D I 是个人经验，没有永久普遍禁令。

questions.passage: Art, he says, “prompts you to stop in your tracks, take a breath and open yourself up so that you can receive what it is offering, often with a kind of childlike awe and reverence…artworks widen your emotional repertoire. When you read a poem or see a piece of sculpture, you haven’t learned a new fact, but you’ve had a new experience.” We can open ourselves up to new experiences not just through reading novels and poems, but also by looking at art.
questions.prompt: What benefit of art does Brooks emphasize?
options: Its value depends entirely on teaching a new factual claim.
It expands emotional experience rather than merely adding facts.
It prevents viewers from responding with awe.
It works only through novels and never through visual art.
questions.promptZh: Brooks 强调艺术什么益处？
optionsZh: 价值完全取决于教会新事实。
扩大情感体验，而不只是增加事实。
阻止观者敬畏。
只靠小说，视觉艺术无效。
analyses: A haven’t learned a new fact...had a new experience 是对照，非事实唯一标准。
B widen your emotional repertoire 概括情绪体验扩展。
C childlike awe 明确允许敬畏。
D sculpture 与 looking at art 包含视觉艺术。引语是观点说明，不是对每个观众必定发生的实测保证。

evidence.quote: artworks widen your emotional repertoire.
you haven’t learned a new fact, but you’ve had a new experience.

vocabulary.meaning: 可运用的范围；积累的储备
vocabulary.context: emotional repertoire 指可感受的情绪范围，不是音乐曲目清单
vocabulary.example: The story widened her emotional repertoire.

questions.translation: 他说，艺术“促使你停下、呼吸、敞开心，接纳它给予的东西，常怀孩子般的惊叹与敬意……作品扩大你的情感范围。读诗或看雕塑，你未必学到新事实，却有了新体验”。不只小说与诗，看艺术也能让我们向新体验敞开。

Visual art makes reading novels and poems impossible.

Art must replace every other activity in a person's life.
